one_line_contribution: That the number of retrieved memory items injected into a ReAct agent is simultaneously a variance lever, so that the fraction of a prompt optimizer's reported validation gain attributable to pure selection bias (measured by a null-proposal optimizer) is strictly larger at k=7 than at k=0 - plus a measurement of whether common random numbers survive interactive rollouts, split into item-sharing and seed-sharing components.
closest_prior_work: Two, and the proposal concedes both. (1) Dodge et al. 2019 'Show Your Work' owns the max-of-N validation inflation mechanism and the 'report performance as a function of search budget' prescription; P7 is literally a fit to sigma*sqrt(2 ln N), i.e. a confirmation of their formula with a measured sigma. (2) The track's own prior work already reported a null replicate matching the best real treatment and a 5-14 point re-scoring spread, which is P6 - correctly demoted to replication. What is left as novel is thinner than it looks: given P1 (sigma rises with k) and the extreme-value account the proposal itself endorses, P2 (bias rises with k) is close to an arithmetic corollary rather than an independent finding, so E1's 76,800 search rollouts are largely spent confirming a two-line derivation. On the remedy side, Miller 2024 ('Adding Error Bars to Evals') already argues for paired/variance-reduced comparison of LLM evaluations and resampling-based power analysis, which pre-empts much of the framing of E2b even if not the interactive-agent CRN decomposition. The genuinely unclaimed object is P3 (does seed-sharing buy anything once a changed prompt changes the tool queries), and that is one experiment, not a paper.
strongest_objection: E0 and E1 cannot attribute variance inflation to memory injection, because injection also moves the mean accuracy and there is no mean-variance decoupling anywhere in the protocol. Scores are binary per item, so sigma is mechanically p(1-p)/m: the track's own prior result says k=7 hurts accuracy, so the predicted sigma(k=7)/sigma(k=0) >= 1.3 in P1 can be produced entirely by the accuracy level drifting toward 0.5, with no 'lengthened and destabilized trajectories' involved at all. The proposal reports mean episode length and tool calls as corroboration but never standardizes the variance (no overdispersion ratio against the binomial baseline at the realized p, no accuracy-matched comparison), so the headline coupling survives its own primary test under an explanation that has nothing to do with memory. The same confound then propagates to P2, since null gain scales with sigma. Second, the primary k-contrast is 4 paired optimizer seeds on run-level null gain, which is itself an extreme-value statistic accumulated over 8 generations of max-of-12; the assumed between-run SD of 1.5 points is optimistic for exactly that kind of quantity, and the proposal's own escape clause (if SD > 2.2, report as directional only) means the most likely outcome of the primary experiment is 'not detected'. Third, curse fraction = null gain / real gain is a ratio with a denominator the authors' own Risk 1 says may be near zero; its 4-seed interval will be unstable or undefined, and P2's 0.15-absolute threshold on it is not defensible.
what_would_fix_it: Add a length- and accuracy-matched placebo injection arm and report variance as an overdispersion ratio relative to p(1-p)/m at the realized accuracy, so that 'volume inflates variance' is separated from 'volume moves accuracy toward 0.5' and from 'more prefill tokens'. Run E1 at k in {0,3,7} rather than {0,7}: prior track work puts the harm threshold between 3 and 7, so a dose-response with the same breakpoint would be real evidence for the coupling, whereas a two-level contrast cannot distinguish dose-response from an idiosyncratic difference between two configurations. Raise E1 to 6-8 optimizer seeds per cell (the cheapest way is fewer generations or a smaller candidate pool, both of which are logged variables in E3 anyway) and pre-register null gain difference in points as the primary endpoint, dropping the curse-fraction ratio to a descriptive secondary. Draw the E2 candidate pool independently of the validation pool used to build the tensor. Finally, demote the EB rank-preservation 'result': shrinkage toward a common mean under equal allocation and equal variances is a monotone affine map of the scores, so rank preservation is a one-line observation, and P5 pre-registers that this claimed contribution is a no-op.
missing_baseline: A placebo injection arm: k=7 items that are token-count-matched but non-informative (shuffled, topically mismatched, or neutral filler distilled to the same length), evaluated in both E0 and E1. Without it, 'memory volume' is confounded with context length and with accuracy level, and a reviewer will read P1/P2 as 'longer prompts make agents noisier', which is neither new nor about memory. Secondarily missing on the remedy side: a plain fresh-validation-split rule (resample the validation pool each generation, or hold out a rotating slice) as the cheapest anti-overfitting control practitioners actually use, and an accuracy-matched k=0 condition (e.g. a weakened seed prompt) that lands at the same p as k=7, to test whether bias tracks injection or merely tracks sigma.
preprint_collision: The check is not thin, it is empty, and by the proposal's own words this is the second consecutive round with zero retrieved titles ('the literature search failed again, and returned nothing... novelty unverified'). The honesty is genuinely creditable - no fabricated citations, an explicit pre-registered query list, and a kill clause if both the k-interaction and the CRN decomposition are already published - but honesty about an unverified claim does not make the claim verified, and after two rounds the burden has not been discharged. The named collisions (Dodge 2019 for the mechanism, the track's own null replicate for P6, ProTeGi/MIPROv2/GEPA for partial mitigations) are all conceded from background knowledge, and the authors themselves flag 2025-2026 preprints on agent evaluation noise floors and winner's-curse corrections for prompt optimizers as the highest-risk unretrieved area. I could not verify that area either within the constraints of this review, so I treat novelty as unestablished rather than absent; note that Miller 2024 on error bars for evals and the general body of work on evaluation-variance quantification already cover part of the remedy framing, which raises the prior that something in the last twelve months covers the selection-bias-in-prompt-optimizers claim as well. This alone would not sink the paper, but combined with the fact that the headline is a corollary of a mechanism the authors disclaim, it means the submission currently rests on P3 - a single negative-result experiment - as its only defensibly unclaimed contribution.
